n01.text: Chimney smoke. Real food. I could weep.

n02.text: You wept at the river too, Gonzō. Over a fish.

n03.text: It was a very good fish.

n04.text: The lanterns aren't lit. It's nearly dark.

n05.text: There now, little one, burn for me... No. Grey again. Lady Benika, is that you? Thank the First Brush.

n06.text: Old Hotaru, why is it grey? The shrine seals should keep every flame red. I checked them myself before I left.

n07.text: Since the new moon, the paper drinks the red like it's thirsty. And the Blot has crept to the bottom of the stair.

n08.text: We came through Sumikage Wood. The birds were painted on the branches mid-song, and none of them moved.

n09.text: Without the lanterns, the things that crawl out of that wood will walk our streets at night.

n10.text: Then they can walk into my staff.

n11.text: And this young man? A stranger, with his hand wrapped.

n12.text: I need somewhere to sleep. Hard to sleep with ink-beasts at the door.

n13.text: Translation: yes, he'll help. He's just bad at saying it.

n14.text: Ha! Then take this. My last good lantern seal, painted before the cracking.

n15.text: It's warm. Like it's still wet. My palm itches.

n16.text: Ink remembers the hand that made it. Find who's breaking the seals, and maybe it'll remember how to hold.

n17.text: Nobody unwrites my town. We go up the stair at first light.

n18.text: After breakfast. Tell me it's after breakfast.

n19.text: Grandmother Tsuru's shop is still open. She'll feed you, if you buy something.

n20.text: First light, then. Let's see what's hungry for ink.

n01.text: Come in, come in. Wipe your feet, the Blot gets everywhere.
Back again? Good. I was starting to worry.
Your purse is lighter than your appetite, dear.
Let's see what you've dragged in.
Fair trade. I'll find it a home.
Mind the stair after dark. And eat something, Gonzō.
Come back alive. I like customers who pay twice.
